Commentary.Commentary: Now, the target is a tricky one and it won't be easy for New Zealand to chase this down. Also, Pakistan have never lost a game in the UAE when they have scored above 130 batting first. So history is favoring them at the moment. But the visitors do have a batting line-up capable of overhauling the target. Who will hold the edge after the first T20I?

The New Zealand bowlers were exceptionally for most parts of the innings. Adam Milne was the pick as he finished with a two-fer. Sodhi was economical and the rest also did well. Their fielding was even better. A special mention to Glenn Phillips who was a live wire out there.

Pakistan at one staged looked like they would struggle to cross the 140-run mark. Especially when Ahmed and Malik both fell in one over. But 25 runs from the last two overs, courtesy Imad Wasim and Faheem Ashraf has seen them finish two runs short of 150.

A strong finish by Pakistan has seen them finish with a total they would be extremely confident of defending. After electing to bat, they did not have a Powerplay to remember as they were 31 for the loss of 2 wickets. Asif Ali and Hafeez then joined forces and added 67 runs. However, just as the two decided to step on the gas, the latter perished 5 short of a half ton. Ali soon followed him and then the runs dried up.

SIX! You bet they can! A maximum to end the innings. 10 from the last two balls and 14 from the final over. Top shot that by Imad. He goes down on one knee and slog sweeps it over the mid-wicket fence. He was helped by Southee as he bowled a full toss but you still got to put it away and he did. PAKISTAN END WITH 148 ON THE BOARD!
FOUR! And they have got it on the penultimate ball. Short and outside off, Wasim smashes it past the bowler and to the long off fence. One ball to go, can Pakistan end it with a bang?
Back of a length on off, Faheem pushes it through covers for a run. Need a boundary here Pakistan.
Lovely stuff! A yorker outside off, can't do a lot with that. Ashraf fails to jam it out.

DROPPED! So after three brilliant catches, New Zealand have put down a sitter. Ish Sodhi is the culprit. Imad tries to play the paddle scoop but there is hardly any pace on the ball. It lobs towards Sodhi at short fine leg. He misjudges it and stops as he is tracking back. Then realises the ball is falling behind him so sticks a hand up and tries to take it with one hand but fails to hang on. A run taken.
Slower ball outside off, Imad hits it through covers, not off the middle but enough to get two.
Tim Southee to bowl the last over.
SIX! HAMMERED! A short ball outside off, Faheem pulls it over mid-wicket for a massive hit! 11 runs from the over, Milne finishes with 2/28 in 4 overs.
A short ball again, but slower in pace, Ashraf looks to pull again but is beaten by the change in pace.
A short ball, pulled through mid-wicket for a couple.
WIDE. Full and down the leg side, FA misses out on the flick.
Outside off, Ashraf tries to ramp it over the keeper but misses.
Outside off, dabbed to third man for a single.

NOT OUT. Waste of the review. Clearly pitching outside leg. No need to check any further. Faheem missed out on the flick shot and was hit on the pads. Adam Milne felt it was out and Williamson went with him. Meanwhile, a leg bye was stolen.
A review for LBW! That seemed to be pitching outside leg to the naked eye. Let's check...
Imad Wasim walks out to the middle. Also, Adam Milne is the new man in.

OUT! A direct hit and Shoaib Malik has been run out! The last thing Pakistan needed. Now 150 seems a touch farfetched. But once again it is an outstanding fielding effort. Anderson pulls out something brilliant for the second time in the space of three balls. Faheem hits it down to long on and the batsmen take a run. Malik wants a second and he rushes towards the other end. Seeing the fielder get to the ball quickly, Ashraf sends Malik back from the point of no return. He turns and also puts in a dive but the direct hit from the deep ensures he has to take the long walk back.
On the pads, worked around the corner for a run.
Faheem Ashraf is the new man in.

OUT! Another superb catch in the field! This time by Anderson. Sodhi gets his revenge. This is floated up on middle, Ahmed dances down the track and tries to go big. He is not to the pitch of the ball but still goes through with the shot. The ball turns away a touch which makes the shot a little more tougher. It takes the top edge and lobs towards long off. Anderson there makes good ground to his right, dives and holds onto it. So New Zealand are taking wickets at regular intervals, the perfect way to stop the run-flow.
SIX! Much, much-needed! Sarfraz brings out the slog sweep, connects well and it sails over the square leg stand for a biggie.
Flatter and outside off, Malik cuts it to point for another single.
A single to start the 18th. New Zealand won't mind that. Short and on middle, it is pulled to deep mid-wicket for a run.
A dot to end! Short and wide outside off, Malik misses the cut shot. So despite a boundary in the over, it only costs 7.

A run out opportunity goes abegging. A reprieve there for Sarfraz. It was short and on middle, again it was the seam up ball. Malik mistimes his pull towards mid-wicket. Ahmed is off for a single but Malik is not interested. Sarfraz tries to get back but is too late. However, to his fortune, Southee fails to collect the throw by the fielder and breaks the stumps with his hands. Sarfraz makes it in safely.
The seam up ball now, Ahmed was not expecting it. He is late onto the shot and it goes towards covers for a run.
A couple now but this is poor from Southee. Can't give so much width with third man up. Outside off, Ahmed plays it square on the off side for a couple.
FOUR! With third man up, any sort of an edge will go to a boundary. Short and slower ball outside off, Ahmed tries to cut but gets an outside edge, past short third man for a boundary.
Another dot! Short and outside off, Ahmed tries to guide it down to third man but is beaten.
Tim Southee back on.
Yes, only a run as Sarfraz guides it down to short third man for a single. 5 from the 16th.
Flatter and on middle, Malik works it through mid-wicket for a run. Can he end this over well?
Just a single! A brilliant over till now. Short and outside off, Ahmed chops it to point for a single.
Makes room and smashes it to covers. A dot, gold at this stage.
Another tossed up ball, Ahmed hits it hard down towards long on. The fielder runs to his left and keeps it to two.
Tosses it up on middle, kept out.
Ish Sodhi is back on.
Fullish and on off, Ahmed times it down to long off for a run. 9 runs from the over but the wicket of the power-hitter as well.
Does the smart thing now, he taps it towards covers and takes a run. Follows the boundary with a single.
FOUR! EDGY AGAIN! Pakistan won't care though. Full and outside off, Malik plays inside the line, the ball takes the outside edge and races to the third man fence.
Back of a length outside off, Ahmed guides it through point for a single.
WIDE! Way down the leg side, Ahmed lets it be.
Shoaib Malik is the new man in.

OUT! In the air...taken! Another ripper of a catch. Glenn Phillips is the man this time. He has been outstanding in the field today. It is once again the slower ball on middle, Ali swings but the ball goes off the inner half towards deep mid-wicket. It is dipping on the fielder. He makes good ground forward, then dives and takes it inches above the surface. Another huge wicket as Asif Ali can be very dangerous at the death. Both the set batsmen now in the hut. Just what New Zealand wanted, especially with only 5 overs to go after this one.
Slower ball on the pads, Sarfraz works it to short fine leg for a run.

A single to finish! So a good comeback by him after going for a boundary. He again fires it very full outside off, Ahmed hits it to sweeper cover for a run. Also, that is the end of his spell. 4-0-27-1 is how his figures reads. Good job by the left-arm spinner.
Makes room but Patel fires a yorker. He jams it out. Two dots in a row.
Flatter and outside off, Ahmed guides it to point.
Works it with the angle through mid-wicket for a run.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot. One run added to the total.
FOUR! Ideal start to the over! That has been swept brilliantly. Down the leg side, Ahmed sweeps it through backward square leg and the ball races away.
Ajaz Patel to bowl out. 3-0-20-1 so far.
7 from the over, a decent one from Colin. Sarfraz eases it down to long off for a run.
FOUR! DEFT! Sarfraz clears his front leg to go over the leg side. The ball though is bowled outside off, Ahmed guides it through backward point for a boundary.
On the pads, the batsman fails to flick it and is hit on the pads.
Fullish and on off, Ali hits it down to long off for a run.
Once again it is flicked off his pads for a run.
On middle, worked to mid-wicket.
Colin de Grandhomme is back on.
Slower ball outside off, Ali tries to cut but is way too early into the shot. A dot to end a successful over.
Outside off, guided down to third man for a run. Ahmed is off the mark.
Sarfraz Ahmed walks out to the middle. He has promoted himself up the order.

OUT! WHAT A CATCH! Tim Southee, you beauty! A much-needed breakthrough for New Zealand and it had to be something special to separate the two. It is short and wide outside off, Hafeez cuts it hard to the left of point. When he hit it, he would have thought there were runs on offer but it was not to be. Southee dives full stretch and takes a blinder. Not easy for the tall man to go down so quickly and grab it. Hafeez' superb knock is over but his partnership with Ali has steadied the ship.
Good comeback by the bowler. Fast and on the stumps, kept out.
EDGY FOUR! Pakistan now getting a move on. Shorter and outside off, Hafeez hops and tries to cut but gets a top edge and into the third man fence.
Slower ball to begin with on the shorter side, Ali mistimes his pull towards mid-wicket for a run.
Adam Milne is back on.
Ends the over with a single. A good one for Pakistan, 11 from it. It is worked through square leg for a run.
The batsman works it down the leg side. They pick up a single.
SIX! Clean as a whistle! How delightful was that shot! Hafeez uses his feet and gets to the pitch of the ball. He nonchalantly hits it over the long on fence for a maximum.
Dances down the track but Patel smartly fires it outside off, Ali hits it towards covers for a run.
Quicker and flatter again on the stumps, giving the batsman no room to play with. Hafeez eases it down to long on for a run.
This is flatter and on middle, it is worked down to long on for a run.
Ajaz Patel is back into the attack.
Gets on the front foot in defense.
SPECTACULAR PHILLIP! A short ball, pulled through mid-wicket. The ball is racing towards the boundary but Glenn Phillips puts in a full-length dive to his left to make a terrific stop.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
WIDE. Well outside off, left alone. THE 50-RUN STAND HAS COME UP WITH THAT.
Thehandsomehunk - 'Hey commentator - seems like you missed about Sodhi's birthday...' @thehandsomehunk - Indeed we have. He has turned 26 today.
Full on middle, flicked straight to mid-wicket for a single.
Short and outside off, cut through the covers for a run.
A short ball, around off, punched towards long on for a single.
SIX! Massive hit! Full and outside off, Asif gets down and mows it over mid-wicket for a biggie!
The batsman has pushed it to the cover region. One run added to the total.
Full on middle, pushed through mid-wicket for a run.
Drives it straight down the ground for a single.
FOUR! Neatly done. Short and outside off, Hafeez cuts it behind point for a boundary!

DROPPED! Colin nearly strikes with his first ball. Full and outside off, Hafeez comes forward to drive but is done in by the lack of pace. He gets a thick outside edge behind but Tim Seifert, standing up to the stumps, is unable to take it.
Another bowling change. Colin Munro to bowl now.
Another punch through the covers for another single.
On middle and leg, flicked away for one.
Punches this towards long on for a run.
Outside off, punched back to the bowler.

OUT? Caught behind? Nope. Excellent umpiring by Shozab Raza. Down the leg side, Hafeez misses his flick and there is a noise as the ball goes past. Tim Seifert collects and immediately goes up in an appeal but the umpire calmly shakes his head. Williamson comes running in for the review but he is suggested by his teammates not to take it. Snickometer shows a spike when the ball passed the pad.
On middle, flicked through mid-wicket for a single. The stand moves to 30 from 24 balls.
First sign of Ish Sodhi.
MISFIELD. By Williamson. A rarity. Full and outside off, driven straight to cover but Kane Williamson misfields and the batsmen take a run.
Full and outside off, stops on the batsman, MH is early into his push and spoons the ball in the air. Luckily for him, it is in the gap at cover and he gets a single.
FOUR! FETCH THAT! Short and it is dispatched. Outside off, pulled with absolute disdain through mid-wicket. Glenn Phillips races to his right, flings himself to try and stop the ball, but in vain.
Gets it wide of the man at short mid-wicket this time and comes back for the second.
Full on middle, flicked straight to short mid-wicket.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
Colin de Grandhomme introduced into the attack now.

Outside off, played straight to short third man. Wants a single but is sent back. Decent over from Southee, apart from that surprising six. Good Powerplay for New Zealand. Just 31 runs conceded, 2 wickets taken and only 5 boundaries given.
A short ball now, pulled to deep mid-wicket for a single.

SIX! Ho ho ho! Hafeez, you beauty! T20 cricket gives no respect to a bowler or a batsman. Southee is a pace bowler but the Professor has toyed with him on this ball, as if he were a school kid. Gets down on a knee and paddles it wayyy over fine leg! Surely Southee would not have expected that, going by the way the previous two balls were played. First biggie of the night. The stand is worth 20 from 15 balls while Hafeez has moved to 15 from 13 balls.
Around off, defended watchfully.
Comes down the track but Southee gives him no room. Is forced to defend.
On middle and leg, pushed towards mid on.
Tim Southee to bowl now.
Another length ball, flayed uppishly towards third man for a run. 10 from that over.
A length ball this time, punched through point but this time Glenn Phillips puts in an outstanding dive to his right to stop the ball.

FOUR! Right from the textbook by the Professor! Short and outside off, plenty of room to free the arms, Hafeez accepts it and crashes it past a diving backward point to the boundary! The stand moves to 13 from 9 balls.
A length ball outside off, generates extra pace and bounce, Hafeez is forced to jump and defend and gets a thick inside edge onto his pads.
Outside off, steered towards third man for a single.
FOUR! FEROCIOUS! Seems he was expecting that short ball. Is camped back in the crease and pulls it in a flash over mid-wicket.
Punches it straight to cover. Just the boundary and a wicket from the over, Ajaz' figures read 2-0-9-1.
FOUR! Fine way to get off the mark. Full and outside off, Hafeez comes down the track and lofts it over cover for a boundary!
Jumps out of his crease this time but is not quite to the pitch of the ball. Mistimes his drive towards mid on.
Much fuller, Hafeez pushes it towards short extra cover.
Pretty straight, blocked back to the bowler.
Here comes the Professor. Mohammad Hafeez is in at number 4, replacing Farhan.

OUT! Straight to the man! The dropped catch does not count and both the openers are back in the hut in the space of 6 balls. MAIDEN T20I WICKET FOR AJAZ PATEL. Full and around off, Farhan gets down and sweeps it hard and in the air. However, it does not have that much power and finds Colin Munro to perfection at deep square leg! The Kiwis are pumped up and why not?
Drives it down the ground for a run. 2 runs and a wicket from Milne's opener.
A rash shot. The length is short, but Farhan pulls without any feet movement and is beaten.
Outside off, on a length, steered to third man for a single.
Around off, defended watchfully.
Asif Ali comes in at number 3, replacing Babar.

OUT! Caught behind! Dear me, Milne has got the Bradman-esque Azam. A short ball outside off, Babar looks to cut but there is steep bounce and pace on that. As a result, he is cramped for room and only manages to get a thick outside edge. Easy catch for Seifert. Body blow for Pakistan.
Short and outside off, extra bounce, played towards backward point.
Adam Milne is brought on.
Looks to flick but the ball goes off the inside edge to short fine leg. He wants a run but is then sent back.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.

DROPPED! Oh dear... would you believe it? A Kiwi has dropped a catch. Replays confirm that the ball went straight into the palms of Adam Milne at mid on, but then dropped down. It was just a chip from Farhan to mid on and should have been taken. No wonder Farhan did not move when the Kiwis were celebrating and the umpires referred it upstairs.
Is that a wicket? Adam Milne has taken the catch but he is not claiming it. The umpires have referred it upstairs and the soft signal is OUT.
Down the leg side, BA misses his flick and the ball goes off his pads through square leg. A leg bye taken.
Lovely shot. Full on middle, Babar drives it straight down the ground for a couple.
A length ball outside off, Azam looks to punch but the ball barely comes off the surface. Takes the inner half and hits him on the pads.
Tim Southee to bowl from the other end.
On middle and leg, flicked straight to short mid-wicket. Excellent comeback from the debutant after going for a boundary on the first ball.
Outside off, punched towards mid on.
Gets it much fuller, it is pushed through mid on for a quick single.
Another cut shot, cannot beat cover once more.
Short again, lucky to get away with it this time. Babar rocks back to cut but finds cover.
FOUR! Bad start for the debutant. It is short and outside off, Azam goes back and punches it through the covers for a boundary!
We are all ready for the game and series to begin. Babar Azam and Sahibzada Farhan are the openers for Pakistan. Debutant Ajaz Patel to start off proceedings to Babar. Here we go!
Time for the national anthems then. New Zealand's first, followed by Pakistan's.

TEAM NEWS - Big one for New Zealand first up. Ajaz Patel is making his international debut. He is a left-arm orthodox spinner. Pakistan have included Shoaib Malik, which is good news for them while Fakhar Zaman continues to be absent due to a knee injury. Shaheen Afridi replaces Usman Khan from the playing XI that featured in the third T20I against Australia.

TOSS - Time for the spin of the coin. PAKISTAN HAVE WON THE TOSS and not surprisingly, WILL BAT FIRST AGAIN. Considering that the pitch slows down considerably in the second innings and also turns, they are seemingly liking the idea of putting a total on the board and then apply pressure on the opposition with their incisive bowling.

A couple of players missing out for both sides, even before the game starts. Martin Guptill has been ruled out of the entire white-ball tour while for Pakistan, Shoaib Malik has just become a father yesterday. That puts his participation tonight in doubt.

We have barely recovered from Australia's drubbing by Pakistan and the former's neighbours are already here. They will be playing 3 T20Is, 3 ODIs and 3 Tests, starting from tonight. The 'hosts' have won their last 10 T20I series on the trot but this one could be a difficult one. The Kiwis will certainly be more competitive than their Trans-Tasman neighbours and we should have good cricketing action. Hello and a warm welcome to the first T20I between Pakistan and New Zealand in Abu Dhabi.
